verses.1: Anah Nevukadnazar Shelah Hovit in my house, and he lights up my room.
verses.2: I dream of visions; they tempt me, and my thoughts wander while I’m lying in bed. My dreams terrify me.
verses.3: And from me, I set the taste for the shoe polish before all the wise men of Babylon. May they know this, O Lord.
verses.4: Bedayin alin harutumaya ashfaya kashdaye vegazraya vehlemaya amara anah kudamihon ufishreha la-mehodain li.
verses.5: And after them, in the time of Daniel the Great, there was Beltsachar, who was named after the god. And the sacred spirits of that god lived there. And before him, Amrēt ruled.
verses.6: Beltshazar Rab Harumaya diya anah yidet diya ruach Elohin Kadoshim baka vekhal-Raz la-Anes laka Chezuy Helyi di-Hazit uPishreha Amar.
verses.7: And my foreheads were on my chests; I saw them lying there. They were like trees in the wilderness, and their branches were high up in the air.
verses.8: Many will be destroyed and their bodies will be thrown onto the ground. They will be seen as worthless in the end.
verses.9: May she be pure and holy, and may her branches bear fruit for all. May her life be full of beauty and joy. And from her branches, birds will sing praises to her. From her roots, everything will grow well.
verses.10: I saw in my dreams, from above my bed, that it was a city and a holy place among the other cities.
verses.11: Read it in verse form. And he said, “They cut down its branches. They stripped it bare. In the darkness, its leaves were torn from its branches.”
verses.12: Its roots lie in the land of Shavku and Esur Di-Farzel. It also includes snakes in the land of Bar’a. And in Tal Shmayya, it becomes fertile. With its life force, it shares its share in the creation of Ar’a.
verses.13: Her heart will be filled with people who change, and her life will be illuminated. Seven dynasties will pass over her.
verses.14: In the general situation of the city, it is said that the sacred ones will speak until they understand what the rulers of Anashah have decided. Then, they will be given a place of honor, and the people will be blessed.
verses.15: Dena Halamah Hazit Anah Malaka Nebukadnetsar, and Anath Beltshatsar Pishra. He said: “All those who receive it, all the wise men of my kingdom, cannot know me. And you, who are like the souls of the holy gods, in you I am.”
verses.16: Eadain Daniyel Di-Shmeh Beltsharz, his wife. At that time, she was in a state of great fear and distress. The king asked her, “Beltsharz, what is your dream?” Beltsharz replied, “My dream is for you to be blessed and happy.”
verses.17: I will see many things that are hidden and secret; they will be revealed in the end. They will be seen by everyone.
verses.18: And let her fly freely, and let her spread her wings wide. May all things be blessed through her. Her branches will provide shelter for birds of the sky.
verses.19: Anth-hu’a malkah di rabbit ut tekafat. Urbuatakh rabbat, ut mtaat li-shmayya. Shaltanakh le-sof ar’a.
verses.20: And God saw a city and a holy place from His throne. He said, “Let them be planted in the land of Ar’a Shvuku and in Esur Di-Parzel. And let snakes live there, along with all those creatures that God created.” Until seven generations pass over it, it will remain a holy place.
verses.21: Dana Pishra Malaka’s rule is a great one; it truly benefits everyone who lives under his reign.
verses.22: And you shall go forth from among the people, with your followers. You will create a path and a way for yourself. May those who follow you be blessed. Seven gates will pass over you until you reach the throne of the king of the people. Then, you will be able to settle down there.
verses.23: And they said to Mishbak, “Your roots are weak. Your kingdom will end soon. You will no longer be able to rule over others.”
verses.24: May the king’s words be a warning to you regarding your sins and wrongdoings. May your downfall come from the hands of the poor people. They will bring you down to your knees.
verses.25: All this is done by Nebuchednazar, the king.
verses.26: A little while ago, there were twelve people who stood before the palace of King David. They were the ones who ruled over the land.
verses.27: The king replied, “No, she is not Babel. She is a woman who was given to me as a wife. She is my beloved, and I love her deeply.”
verses.28: Once again, from the mouth of the king, it is said that he has fallen from his throne. May the king’s kingdom be destroyed by you.
verses.29: And from among the people of Anashah, there will be those who lead you along a path of thorns. They will create a difficult journey for you. Seven nations will pass by you until you understand what the ruler of Anashah has planned for you.
verses.30: At that time, there would be no furniture on Nebukadnezar’s palace. People would be displaced and scattered everywhere. The ground would be covered with corpses, so many that they would cover the entire area like a thick blanket.
verses.31: And for a little while, I will be like Nabuchadnezzar. I will take control of everything and rule over all things. May there be blessings upon me forever, and may my kingdom last forever.
verses.32: And all the nations of the world are considered important. They serve under the command of Shemaya. But those nations do not have any control over him; they cannot say, “What do you do?”
verses.33: In this time of need, may they be merciful to me. May they protect my kingdom from destruction. May they also protect my words and my teachings. May my friends stand by me, and may my kingdom be established once more.
verses.34: May he be praised, honored, and glorified by the king of all his servants. May his reign be long and prosperous. May those who go forth in his name be able to triumph over all obstacles.
